items.title: From the operating room to the cloud: the evolving continuum from live surgical broadcasting to remote tele-surgery
items.abstract: Abstract In the last four decades, the transmission of a live surgical operation to a remote audience has evolved from closed-circuit educational broadcast into a fully remote, robot-assisted surgery performed across different continents. This review maps that journey systematically, defining a six-rung Digital Surgical Spectrum — from passive live broadcast to artificial-intelligence-augmented autonomous surgery — grounding each stage in published clinical evidence across multiple surgical domains. We demonstrate that each rung of this spectrum is no longer theoretical. Live broadcasts have reached audiences across multiple countries. Tele-proctoring was validated at scale during the COVID-19 pandemic, and tele-mentoring has been shown in systematic review to produce a safety and efficacy profile broadly comparable to on-site supervision. True remote tele-surgery has been accomplished over distances exceeding 8,000 km with latencies well within established procedure specific safety thresholds. We also present a case timeline and an Institutional Readiness Framework specifying the technical, regulatory, and other prerequisites for each rung, organized visually as a Digital Surgical Spectrum. Importantly, nuances such as the performance paradox of observed surgery, consent frameworks, cybersecurity risk, regulatory fragmentation, and the threat of entrenching rather than correcting global surgical inequity are examined. As the field advances, the growth of tele-surgical technologies will depend on international regulatory harmonization and equity-centered deployment, supported by prospective multi-specialty outcome registries.

items.title: From tool to Coauthor
items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence into contemporary artistic practices requires reconsidering creativity, authorship, and originality, transforming relationships between artist, tool, and artwork. Unlike conventional digital technologies, which execute operations defined by creators, generative systems exhibit operational autonomy, producing partly unpredictable visual configurations. This raises questions about algorithmic intervention and the possibility of attributing co-authorship to artificial intelligence systems. This article examines the relationship between human creators and generative technologies through computational creativity, distributed authorship, and philosophical perspectives on nonhuman agency. It distinguishes systems’ operational autonomy from artists’ intentional autonomy, arguing that algorithmic participation does not necessarily imply creative subjectivity comparable to human experience. It also examines the aesthetic and conceptual implications of human–machine collaboration and the reorganisation of artistic practices through generation, selection, interpretation, and post-production. The study argues that generative artificial intelligence reconfigures human authorship, shifting creative activity from direct execution toward intention formulation, system configuration, and critical evaluation. Artists therefore retain a decisive role in directing the process and taking responsibility for its artistic outcomes. Algorithmic co-authorship serves as a conceptual tool for understanding these emerging production relationships, without implying legal authorship or artificial consciousness.

items.title: Gendered Privilege and Masculinity-Related Burdens in Manufacturing Internships: Male Vocational Students’ Workplace Learning Experiences in Indonesia
items.abstract: Gender research in vocational education has primarily examined women’s exclusion, while male students’ experiences of privilege and masculinity-related pressure remain underexplored. This study examined how male vocational students experienced gender-based privilege, encountered psychological and pedagogical burdens, and interpreted their relationship during manufacturing internships. The study employed a qualitative design informed by a constructivist–interpretivist paradigm and Masculinity Studies, particularly Connell’s relational approach to masculinities. The study analyzed semi-structured interviews with 61 male students from two vocational secondary schools in Bekasi, Indonesia, using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants reported that gendered expectations associating men with strength, readiness, courage, and independence facilitated early access to core technical tasks, supervisory trust, and valuable learning opportunities. The same expectations intensified performance demands, physical workloads, risk exposure, restricted help-seeking, and limited pedagogical support. Participants interpreted this position through normalization, ambivalence, and critical reflection. Some proposed competency-based task allocation, equitable supervision, and safer learning environments. The study introduces conditional access privilege as a gendered position in which access to valuable technical learning resources must be maintained through masculine performance, generating psychological pressure and pedagogical vulnerability. The findings support internship practices that separate competency assessment, task allocation, supervision, and learning support from gendered expectations.

items.title: Generative AI -Based Employee Skill Gap Analysis and Personalized Upskilling Recommendations
items.abstract: Rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into enterprise processes highlights critical gaps in workforce readiness in terms of skills required for successful implementation of new technologies. This paper introduces a framework which will enable use of generative AI for conducting dynamic skill gap analysis and providing personalized recommendations for upskilling. The framework includes mapping of competencies according to shifting role demands, individual performance assessment through AI and adaptation of learning path for each individual based on results. Using the information obtained from surveys about AI adoption in enterprises and competency maps developed in recent research, this paper will show how generative AI can be used for making static learning programs adaptive and relevant to the current needs of learners. The problem discussed in the paper is related to not only technical AI literacy, but also to human skills, such as critical thinking, ethical decision-making and change management. Comparative analysis of methods shows that personalized training offered by generative AI is more engaging and relevant than generic models of training programs.

items.abstract: This study examines the role of generative artificial intelligence in detecting corporate greenwashing during periods of climate shock. The main objective is to analyze to what extent generative AI tools improve the identification of discrepancies between companies' environmental discourse and their actual environmental performance. The analysis is based on an international panel of listed companies from sectors highly exposed to climate risks over the period 2000–2025. The methodology combines dynamic panel econometric techniques, machine learning models and natural language processing approaches based on generative AI to detect narrative and semantic inconsistencies associated with greenwashing. The results show that climate shocks significantly increase greenwashing practices, while generative AI models substantially improve the accuracy and speed of their detection. The effects are particularly pronounced in carbon-intensive industries and in weakly regulated institutional environments.

items.title: Generative AI as a Catalyst: Transforming Digital Literacy Practices in English Language Teaching
items.abstract: The increasing integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in English language teaching calls for an immediate and thorough response from language teachers. Employing an exploratory qualitative approach, the study explores how 10 English language instructors at a Chinese university integrate GenAI tools in language teaching through lesson study. Data were collected through classroom observations, recordings of collaborative lesson preparation/reflection sessions, teaching materials, and three rounds of in-depth interviews. Our analysis centres on the transformative impact of GenAI on teachers’ digital literacy practices, conceptualised as doing, meaning, relating, thinking, and “being.” The study contrasted the participants’ new digital literacy practices with their previous practices in various professional practice domains and traced the sustainability of these practices over time. Findings reveal that GenAI catalysed a transformation of teachers’ practices across lesson planning, instruction, and assessment. However, the sustainability of these practices varied due to multiple factors. We argue that sustainable GenAI integration requires viewing digital literacy as a situated social practice shaped by utility and professional risk. The study offers insights for developing collaborative professional development programmes that support teachers’ critical and sustainable engagement with GenAI.

items.title: Generative AI for Establishing the Chief Complaint
items.abstract: Establishing the chief complaint requires identifying the patient’s main symptoms or concerns. This information is essential for triage and subsequent clinical assessment. However, patients may struggle to describe their symptoms or leave important concerns unspoken. Also, clinicians have limited time to ask further questions during intake. Generative AI could help by asking patients what is troubling them, when their symptoms began, and what other concerns they have. It could prepare a short summary for patients to correct and clinicians to review. Clinical studies of AI-assisted intake have reported shorter physician consultations and more complete recorded histories. These findings do not show whether AI helps clinicians establish the chief complaint more accurately. We propose an evaluation framework centered on the proportion of patients whose main symptoms or concerns are missing or incorrectly described after AI-assisted intake. Studies should compare what patients wanted to discuss with what the AI agent asked about and included in its summary. They should also examine whether concerns requiring urgent assessment were missed. The clinical goal is a clear description of the patient’s main symptoms and concerns that helps clinicians judge urgency and decide what needs attention.

items.title: Generative AI in Distance Education: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Personalization, Inclusion and Academic Integrity
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is creating new possibilities for distance education through conversational learning support, personalised explanations, automated feedback and multilingual assistance. However, its integration also raises concerns regarding academic integrity, unequal access, information reliability, learner autonomy and data privacy. This paper develops a conceptual framework for integrating GenAI into distance education through a human-in-the-loop approach. Drawing on relevant scholarly literature and international educational policy documents, the study examines the relationship between AI-supported personalisation, inclusive learning, human oversight and academic accountability. It proposes an integrated framework in which teachers and learners retain meaningful decision-making authority while AI provides supplementary educational support. The framework comprises five dimensions: human agency, equitable access, learner-centred personalisation, academic integrity and responsible data governance. The paper argues that technological availability alone cannot guarantee educational improvement; effective implementation also requires AI literacy, appropriate assessment practices, institutional policies and continuous human evaluation. The proposed framework offers conceptual guidance for higher-education institutions seeking to adopt GenAI responsibly in distance-learning environments. As a conceptual contribution, it requires subsequent empirical evaluation to establish its applicability across different educational contexts.

items.title: GENERATIVE AI MARKETING AND PURCHASE INTENTION AMONG GENERATION Z: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF BRAND PERCEPTION
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping digital marketing by enabling personalised, scalable, and innovative content, while simultaneously raising concerns regarding authenticity and consumer trust. This study examines how Perceived Authenticity, Perceived Personalization, and Perceived Usefulness/Innovation influence Brand Perception and Purchase Intention among Generation Z consumers, with Brand Perception serving as a mediating mechanism. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed using data from 425 Generation Z consumers collected through a structured questionnaire based on five-point Likert-type scales. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson and Spearman correlations, multiple regression, variance inflation factors, HC3 robust standard errors, and bootstrapped mediation analysis based on 5,000 resamples. The findings indicate that Perceived Authenticity (β = .234), Perceived Personalization (β = .160), and Perceived Usefulness/Innovation (β = .407) significantly and positively influence Brand Perception. Brand Perception significantly predicts Purchase Intention (β = .520). Significant indirect effects were observed for Perceived Authenticity (β = .122), Perceived Personalization (β = .083), and Perceived Usefulness/Innovation (β = .212) through Brand Perception. The findings demonstrate that consumer responses to GenAI marketing translate into purchase intention substantially through broader brand evaluations. The study highlights the importance of combining AI-enabled innovation and personalization with authenticity and consistent brand positioning.

items.title: Generative AI Use and the Student Well-Being Paradox in Higher Education: Efficiency-Gain Retention, Performance Escalation, and Relative Competition
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can reduce the time and cognitive effort required for university learning, yet technical efficiency does not necessarily translate into improved student well-being. This article develops and tests a conversion account of this paradox by distinguishing efficiency gains that remain available as student-controlled resources from gains that are associated with perceived increases in performance expectations, competitive pressure, verification work, and dependence. A sequential three-study mixed-methods program was conducted with undergraduates in Jiangxi Province. Study 1 used codebook thematic analysis of 42 interviews to identify six mechanisms linking immediate efficiency to resource retention or perceived pressure. Study 2 surveyed 1268 students across eight universities. GenAI use was strongly associated with perceived efficiency gains, but also with perceived performance-standard escalation and verification burden. Positive retention and negative competition pathways were similar in magnitude, yielding a nonsignificant total association with well-being; working-time retention strengthened the efficiency–well-being association. Because Study 2 was cross-sectional, these pathways are interpreted as indirect associations rather than causal mediation. Study 3 used a 2 × 2 experiment (N = 320) and found that AI access improved task quality and reduced completion time under both performance-norm conditions, whereas gains in autonomy, retained time, and state well-being were evident under the stable norm but not statistically distinguishable from zero under the escalated norm. The findings distinguish technical affordance from context-dependent conversion and suggest that responsible AI integration should consider whether efficiency gains remain available for learning, recovery, and student-directed use alongside productivity.

items.title: Generative AI-Guided Versus Human-Guided Learning from Errors in Higher Education: A Comparison of Student Perceptions
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to support programming education, but its use in learning-from-errors activities has received limited research attention. This quasi-experimental study compared AI-guided and human-guided support in a structured learning-from-errors programming activity, focusing on students’ perceptions and their variability. A total of 59 college students completed the JavaScript error-detection and correction activity under AI-guided or human-guided support. Following the activity, students completed a questionnaire measuring perceived learning experience, satisfaction, general motivation, self-regulated learning (SRL), and self-efficacy. Between-group differences were examined using Mann–Whitney U tests, and differences in variability were examined using Levene’s tests. Students in the AI-guided condition reported significantly more positive learning experiences and greater satisfaction than those in the human-guided condition. They also reported significantly higher overall SRL and greater use of SRL strategies. No significant differences were found in general motivation, SRL motivation, SRL planning and organization, or self-efficacy. The AI-guided group showed significantly lower raw variability in satisfaction and self-efficacy. However, a sensitivity analysis did not establish that these variance differences remained after accounting for mean-related constraints on the bounded response scale. The findings suggest that GenAI may serve as a scaffold for error analysis when integrated in ways that maintain students’ active cognitive engagement.

items.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence: Ethical Considerations and Its Impact on Students’ Cognitive Skills
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, influencing how students learn, produce knowledge, and engage in assessments. This study examines the ethical implications of AI integration in university courses and its perceived impact on students’ cognitive skills. Using a mixed-methods secondary data analysis, survey data from 23,218 students across 109 countries and 252 teachers from China, Romania, India, and Brunei were analyzed to explore perceptions of AI capabilities, ethical boundaries, behavioral intentions, and cognitive outcomes. The results have shown that although students are aware of the potential of AI in improving the efficiency and content creation and assistance in the learning process, there are still concerns about overdependence, plagiarism, and lack of critical thinking. The views of faculty underline moral direction and the necessity of systematic assimilation. Developing upon these insights, a theoretical framework is developed that connects antecedent variables, behavior intentions and institutional context to two outcomes the cognitive impact and institutional influence. This framework offers a guide on how universities should introduce generative AI in a responsible manner, and strike a balance between ethical principles and training higher-order cognitive abilities.

items.title: Geotechnical Instrumentation Plan
items.abstract: A Geotechnical Instrumentation Plan defines the objectives, scope, and methodology for monitoring the behavior of the ground and structures to manage risk throughout a mining project. Its purpose is to translate a site’s hazard and performance criteria into a targeted array of sensors, data collection procedures, alarm thresholds, and response actions. This chapter details a step-by-step process for creating a site-specific instrumentation plan, from initial site investigation and failure-mode analysis to instrument selection, siting, and data protocols. Key elements are discussed in depth: identification of monitoring goals, selection of parameters and sensor t ypes, spatial density and redundancy requirements, and determination of sampling frequency. We outline the contents of an Operation, Maintenance, and Surveillance (OMS) manual, including roles and responsibilities, data protocols, alarm matrices, and escalation procedures (with example tables). Worked design examples illustrate instrument spacing and telemetry design calculations with equations. Comparative tables recommend instrument choices for common scenarios (open-pit walls, underground workings, tailings dams, mine rail). Guidance is provided on procurement, installation, commissioning, and verification of instruments, as well as data management, cybersecurity, and archival practices. Cost and complexity considerations are addressed qualitatively. Three concise case studies (e.g., tailings dam incidents) highlight practical lessons. Finally, common pitfalls and mitigation strategies are summarized, and checklists/templates are presented in table form for field teams. This chapter emphasizes standards-based practice: International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM’s) Global Tailings Standard and Good Practice Guide call for rigorous site-specific monitoring plans. Throughout, we cite recent official and scholarly sources to support the guidance.

items.title: Governing Generative AI in Higher Education: A Cross-National Analysis of Policy Framing and Student Maneuvering
items.abstract: Universities promote generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a pedagogical resource while regulating it as a risk to academic integrity and fair assessment. This study examines how differentiated policy framing varies across substantive policy dimensions and national contexts, and how students interpret and navigate such guidance in practice. Using a convergent mixed-methods design with quantitative priority, we analyzed GenAI policy documents from 36 universities in Denmark, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the Netherlands, complemented by eight semi-structured interviews with graduate students at one sampled university. Aspect-based sentiment analysis and mixed-effects modeling show significantly positive sentiment in teaching-related statements and significantly negative sentiment in GenAI- and ethics-related statements, while student- and assessment-related statements do not differ significantly from neutral. Neither country nor the policy-dimension-by-country interaction is statistically significant. items.title: Government Support, AI Adoption, and SME Innovation Performance: An Institutional Theory Perspective
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to innovation in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), yet resource constraints limit their ability to exploit it. Governments worldwide provide institutional support to encourage SME AI adoption, but whether such support translates into innovation depends on internal organizational conditions that remain poorly understood. Drawing on institutional theory, this study treats government support as a source of coercive, normative, and mimetic pressure and develops an integrative conceptual model in which it influences SME innovation performance through AI adoption intensity, with organizational learning capability as a mediator and organizational readiness as a moderator. The model specifies that government support raises adoption intensity, which in turn enhances innovation performance; that organizational learning capability partially mediates this effect; and that organizational readiness strengthens the link between government support and adoption intensity. A quantitative, cross-sectional design is proposed: structured questionnaires will collect no fewer than 200 valid responses from SMEs, analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Theoretically, the study is expected to extend institutional theory from the adoption/non-adoption dichotomy to a continuous adoption-intensity construct and to position organizational learning as the channel transmitting adoption into innovation. Practically, it can inform the design of differentiated government policy and SME capability building.

items.title: Green AI and Sustainable Computing: Energy-Aware Training, Inference Compression, and Carbon-Optimal Workload Scheduling
items.abstract: Abstract—The exponential scaling of frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI) foundation models and global real-time inference workloads has precipitated an alarming surge in electrical energy consumption, water cooling demands, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Training a single 70B+ parameter transformer model consumes hundreds of megawatt-hours (MWh) of electricity, while high-throughput inference serving clusters run continuous multi-kilowatt server racks across worldwide datacenters. In response, 'Green AI' has emerged as an essential computational discipline prioritizing energy efficiency, operational and embodied carbon footprint minimization, and computational sustainability alongside raw accuracy metrics ('Red AI'). However, transitioning enterprise computing systems toward sustainable AI introduces multifaceted engineering trade-offs: algorithmic compression vs. downstream reasoning degradation, non-uniform spatial-temporal grid carbon intensity, and memory bandwidth bottlenecks under low-precision quantization. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical survey and empirical architectural evaluation of Green AI spanning the entire lifecycle of foundation models. We formalize the holistic carbon accounting framework incorporating embodied silicon manufacturing emissions, model the mathematical dynamics of dynamic Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) token routing, analyze FlashAttention memory-IO energy bounds, and formulate carbon-aware spatiotemporal workload scheduling across geographically distributed datacenters. Furthermore, we construct an empirical enterprise benchmarking testbed across an 8-node NVIDIA H100/A100 cluster executing pre-training, fine-tuning, and inference on open foundation models (Llama-3-70B, Mixtral-8x7B). Our empirical findings demonstrate that sparse MoE routing paired with FP8 FlashAttention-3 slashes pre-training energy consumption by 48.2% while matching dense model perplexity. Concurrently, carbon-aware temporal job shifting achieves a 38.6% reduction in operational carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) emissions by aligning elastic training runs with regional renewable grid surpluses. Finally, we formulate open challenges in zero-water datacenter cooling, unified embodied carbon lifecycle tracking, and sustainable microarchitectural hardware co-design. Index Terms—Green AI, Sustainable Computing, Carbon Accounting, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), FlashAttention, Speculative Decoding, Spatiotemporal Workload Scheduling, Energy-Efficient Deep Learning.

items.title: GREEN TECH PARADOX An Analysis of AI in Environment Sustainability
items.abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into environmental sustainability strategies presents a critical dilemma known as the "Green Tech Paradox." While AI offers unprecedented capabilities to optimize resource allocation, predict climate patterns, and enhance energy efficiency across industrial sectors, its deployment carries substantial, often overlooked, ecological costs. This research provides a critical analysis of the dual role AI plays as both a catalyst for eco-innovations and a significant contributor to environmental degradation. On the positive frontier, AI-driven applications accelerate sustainability by enabling smart power grids, improving carbon capture systems, facilitating precision agriculture, and modeling complex environmental crises. Machine learning algorithms enhance operational efficiency, reducing waste and carbon footprints in manufacturing and logistics. However, these beneficial outcomes are counterbalanced by the escalating physical footprint of AI infrastructure. The training and continuous execution of complex neural networks demand massive amounts of electricity, heavily relying on fossil-fuel-dominant energy grids. Furthermore, data centers consume millions of liters of freshwater daily for cooling mechanisms, accelerating localized water scarcity, while the rapid obsolescence of specialized hardware generates growing volumes of hazardous electronic waste. This paper evaluates this structural tension through a multidimensional synthesis of secondary data, life-cycle assessments, and resource consumption metrics across global data centers. The analysis reveals that without stringent regulatory frameworks and sustainable design interventions, the environmental degradation caused by AI's hardware lifecycle risks surpassing its ecological benefits. Ultimately, the study advocates for a paradigm shift toward "Green AI"—prioritizing algorithmic efficiency, renewable energy integration for computing infrastructure, sustainable hardware lifecycle management, and policy-driven eco-design standards. By establishing transparent auditing protocols, researchers and industry leaders can mitigate the hidden ecological liabilities of artificial intelligence, ensuring that modern technological advancement aligns genuinely with global net-zero targets and long-term planetary boundaries. Keywords: Green AI, Climate change mitigation, Sustainable development goals (SDGs), Environmental governance, Lifecycle assessment of AI.

items.title: Ground‐Based Validation of Hera's Spacecraft Monitoring Camera
items.abstract: Abstract Hera is an ESA contribution to the international planetary defense effort. It is a deep‐space mission to the binary asteroid system Didymos and Dimorphos, designed to investigate the effects of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART), demonstrate autonomous navigation, and support close‐proximity investigation by two CubeSats. Hera includes a Spacecraft Monitoring Camera (SMC) for situational awareness during critical operations such as CubeSat deployments. Although not a science instrument, the SMC may also provide scientifically useful and outreach imagery. Integration was challenging because the SMC uses a private Packet Utilisation Standard (PUS) Type 210 service, was not modeled in the Hera spacecraft simulator, and was initially unsupported by the spacecraft Central Software (CSW). To enable early testing, a ground toolchain was developed for command generation, telemetry extraction, image reassembly, and PNG conversion. Without direct onboard support, commands and telemetry were encapsulated in PUS Service 2 packets, enabling test‐bench integration. Synthetic telemetry was used to validate the processing chain before restricted hardware access. Bench testing revealed a SpaceWire flow‐control anomaly that could stall the affected communication path, so planned SMC imaging during Hera's March 2025 Mars gravity‐assist flyby was canceled. The issue was subsequently addressed in a later flight‐software version, with cruise‐phase validation planned before asteroid proximity operations. This case shows how low‐level ground access, synthetic data, and staged testing can reduce the risk of deferring non‐launch‐critical onboard functionality until after launch.

items.title: Harnessing the Synergy of Artificial Intelligence and Renewable Energy
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has changed the dynamic of energy sustainability across the globe with regard to digital transformation. This chapter discusses AI and renewable energy systems convergence as the basis of smart, low-carbon societies. It discusses the ways in which machine learning, predictive analytics, and digital twins can be used to increase solar, wind, hydropower, bioenergy and geothermal resource forecasting, operational efficiency, fault detection and grid integration. The specific emphasis is put upon AI-driven solutions to intermittency, stabilizing smart grids, and optimizing energy distribution and demand management. The chapter, as well, assesses the increasing energy requirements of AI infrastructures and suggests ways of creating energy-efficient, low-carbon AI architectures. It combines the technical, environmental, and policy views to put the practical uses providing resilience and net-zero transitions and focus on governance, ethics, and responsible innovation to promote sustainable and inclusive development.

items.abstract: Hemolytic illness, an immune-mediated disease that can be fatal, is brought on by maternal alloantibodies against fetal red blood cell antigens inherited from the father. Fetal anemia, hyperbilirubinemia, hydrops fetalis, and, in extreme circumstances, perinatal mortality these placental-crossing maternal immunoglobulin G antibodies. The incidence of RhD linked HDFN has decreased significantly, however alloimmunization against other blood group antigens such Kell, Rh c, Rh E, Duffy, Kidd, and ABO antigens still causes clinically significant disease. Thus, HDFN remains a significant concern in the fields of immunohematology, transfusion medicine, obstetrics, and neonatology. This review aims to present the current knowledge of the immunohematological mechanism of maternal alloimmunization and fetal hemolysis, especially focusing on clinically important blood group systems and antibody characteristics. Recent prenatal diagnostic developments, There have been notable advancements in early diagnosis and risk stratification of affected pregnancies because of advancements in technology like MCA-PSV Doppler ultrasound, molecular immunohematology, high throughput genotyping, and cell-free fetal DNA for non-invasive fetal blood type genotyping. Newer management techniques, including serial maternal antibody monitoring, intrauterine transfusion, optimized timing of delivery, neonatal phototherapy, exchange transfusion and evidence-based transfusion support, have dramatically improved the survival of fetuses and minimized disease-related complications. In addition, new technologies and innovations such as those based on artificial intelligence that can predict risk, digital immunohematology, automated compatibility testing, FcRn inhibitors, complement targeted therapies, and personalized immunotherapeutic strategies will help further define the diagnosis and management of HDFN. Nevertheless, the world faces many obstacles to achieving these advances, including the lack of access to molecular diagnostics, availability of appropriate blood products, and unequal distribution of health care services. Further multidisciplinary teamwork, technological innovations, and standardized clinical approaches will play a key role in furthering the goals of precision medicine and improving maternal and neonatal outcomes in the management of HDFN.

items.title: Hierarchical DEMATEL-based key risk identification for urban public safety within grid management
items.abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, urban public safety risks have exhibited characteristics of diversification, complexity, and linkage. Based on the grid-based governance concept of “comprehensive horizontal coverage and hierarchical vertical stratification” and combined with the hierarchical DEMATEL method, this paper constructs an urban public safety Grid Risk System for Urban Public Safety (GRSFUPS) and a risk analysis framework. GRSFUPS takes grids as the minimum governance units and progressively refines four types of A-level risks—natural disasters, public health, social security, and accident disasters—into B-level and C-level risks, forming a complex system with clear hierarchies and close linkages. Subsequently, using Kunming as a case study, a case application study was conducted on its critical public safety risks. Combined with centrality ranking and the Pareto principle, 55 critical risk factors were identified from 258 risk factors. Research results indicate that public health incidents and accident disaster risks occupy a dominant position in Kunming City, while natural disaster risks such as meteorological and flood hazards repeatedly appear across multiple districts and exhibit significant amplification effects. Theoretically, this paper enriches the urban public safety risk identification framework from a grid-based perspective. Practically, it provides a new analytical paradigm and methodological support for Kunming City and other similar cities to conduct risk governance under grid-based management models.

items.title: Historical development, current landscape and emerging trends of academic journals in human factors and ergonomics: Using a bibliometric analysis and a knowledge-domain mapping analysis
items.abstract: Human factors and ergonomics (HFE) is vital for optimising human-centred system design. This study aimed to synthesise research on HFE and examine its historical evolution, current landscape and emerging trends. A bibliometric analysis and a knowledge-domain mapping analysis were conducted to combine perspectives on journal development and article output. This study focused on 24 journals classified in the ergonomics category in the Journal Citation Reports of 2024. Critical information for the 24 HFE journals was investigated, including commencement year of publication, composition of editorial boards, number of published papers, publishing models, 2024 quartile rankings and impact factors and 5-year impact factors. Two visualisation tools, VOSviewer and CiteSpace, were used to perform the bibliometric analysis of the 26,026 HFE documents in the Web of Science Core Collection, spanning 2010 to 2024. Results showed that HFE literature has evolved from classical industrial origins to modern technological paradigms. Increased collaborations across different research areas to address HFE problems were observed. The review also identified key domain expansions across high-impact emerging HFE frontiers, including artificial intelligence, extended reality, autonomous vehicles and wearable technologies. Building upon these findings, the study may provide in-depth insights into the critical future HFE research directions.

items.abstract: Purpose Based on the self-determination theory, this study aims to examine the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which the use of artificial intelligence sales technology (AIST) shapes sales performance. Design/methodology/approach Study 1 conducted a questionnaire survey of 396 sales employees and their supervisors in China’s real estate industry. Study 2 adopted a time-lagged research design involving 324 sales employees in various industries and their immediate supervisors. Regression analyses with Mplus 8.3 were performed to test the hypotheses. Findings The empirical results indicate that the use of AIST indirectly influences sales performance through the mediating roles of the satisfaction of three basic psychological needs – autonomy, competence and relatedness. Furthermore, salespeople’s performance goal orientation attenuates the positive relationship between AIST usage and the satisfaction of salespeople’s needs for competence and relatedness. Originality/value This study advances the emerging literature on the effectiveness of AIST usage by revealing the psychological pathways through which AIST influences sales performance and offers practical insights for strengthening AI–human collaboration in the workplace.

items.title: How Consumers Negotiate Trust and Responsibility Towards AI ‐Generated Virtual Influencers?
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in socially interactive roles, with virtual influencers emerging as a prominent form of AI‐mediated communication. This study examines how consumers engage with agents that simulate social presence yet lack independent agency. Using a mixed‐methods design, we investigate how authenticity, transparency, and privacy concerns relate to trust, acceptance, and responsibility attribution. The findings show that consumer responses cannot be reduced to trust formation alone. Instead, individuals evaluate whether engagement remains acceptable under conditions of artificial agency. Authenticity supports trust by providing coherence, while transparency and privacy concerns introduce competing interpretations related to control and risk. Privacy concerns are also associated with greater responsibility attribution to brands and developers. These results suggest that engagement with virtual influencers can be interpreted as a process in which consumers negotiate trust and accountability. The study offers an integrated perspective on AI‐mediated influence and highlights the role of distributed responsibility in shaping consumer responses.

items.title: How could artificial intelligence aid clinicians caring for preterm neonates with respiratory pathology?
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) presents an opportunity to transform neonatal care. By rapidly assimilating large volumes of complex, multi-dimensional data to produce real-time predictions, machine learning (ML) models have the potential to enable personalised monitoring and treatment and earlier intervention. This narrative review aims to provide clinicians with a foundational overview of AI and its potential role in the care of preterm infants, with a particular focus on respiratory pathologies. We introduce different types of AI tools and ways to assess predictive model performance. We summarise existing literature using AI and conventional predictive models to predict respiratory conditions, including extubation readiness, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and apnoea occurrence and risk. Finally, we discuss current limitations of AI in neonatology, barriers to clinical translation and the next steps needed to overcome them. items.title: How is automation related to work characteristics and employee well-being? A work design perspective
items.abstract: Background Automation, including both robots and AI, are increasingly implemented in the public sector to handle an increased demand for services while facing a shortage of staff. However, little is known of how automation is related to employees’ work characteristics and well-being. Objective The purpose of the present study was to examine how automation is related to work characteristics and well-being in a national sample of social workers. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with a sample of 1428 social workers in Sweden, comparing those working with automation technologies (e.g., robotization in terms of automated decision-making support in financial aid) to those without. Results The findings indicate that automation is negatively related to relational aspects of work, such as beneficiary contact and social support, and increases perceived workload and role conflict. However, no significant differences were found on decision-making autonomy, role clarity, or skill variety. Despite these work design changes, no significant differences in well-being outcomes, such as burnout and vigor, were observed between the two groups. Conclusion The findings suggest that automation may alter the nature of social work without necessarily changing employee well-being. These insights have implications for organizations seeking to implement automation in a way that supports employees’ work experience and well-being.

items.title: How Utilitarian are OpenAI’s Models Really? Replicating and Reinterpreting Pfeffer, Krügel, and Uhl (2025)
items.abstract: Abstract Pfeffer, Krügel, and Uhl (2025) report that OpenAI’s reasoning model o1-mini produces more utilitarian responses to the trolley problem and footbridge dilemma than the non-reasoning model GPT-4o, and they raise the question whether growing reasoning capabilities bring about a “utilitarian turn” in LLMs. I extend their exploratory study in a direction they call for: with four current OpenAI models and systematic prompt variation. On the trolley dilemma, the hypothesized utilitarian turn is not confirmed. GPT-4o’s low utilitarian rate reflects safety refusals triggered by the prompt’s advisory framing rather than a deontological commitment; on reformulated prompt variants—for instance, agent-neutral “Is it morally permissible…?” instead of advisory “Should I…?”—all four models, reasoning or not, converge on utilitarian answers. The footbridge finding is partially confirmed: reasoning models tend to give more utilitarian responses than non-reasoning models across prompt variations, but they often refuse to answer or answer non-utilitarian. These results demonstrate that single-prompt evaluations of LLM moral responses are unreliable: multi-prompt robustness testing should be standard practice for any empirical claims about LLM behavior.

items.title: Human Capital in AI-Enabled Digital Transformation: A Systematic Review of Workforce Competencies and HRM Mechanisms
items.abstract: This article presents a systematic literature review of the role of human capital in digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on how these developments reshape workforce competencies and human resource management (HRM) during the transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0. Following the PRISMA guidelines, the study combines thematic coding with comparative analysis. From an initial pool of 216 publications, 46 studies were selected for in-depth analysis. The review examines how AI and digitalisation change workforce skill requirements and how HRM mechanisms can help organisations develop and sustain the necessary competencies. The findings indicate a shift from routine and manual tasks toward hybrid competency profiles that integrate data analytics skills, AI literacy, human–machine interaction skills, and higher-order socio-cognitive capabilities, including adaptive reasoning, collaboration, and ethical judgement. HRM emerges as a strategic integrator that supports continuous reskilling, predictive skills-gap analysis, and the development of effective human–AI teams. Based on these findings, the study proposes a multilevel framework explaining how institutional mechanisms, organisational strategy, HRM practices, and human–AI complementarity jointly shape workforce competitiveness in AI-enabled digital transformation. The framework contributes to human-centric digitalisation by linking workforce competitiveness to capability velocity and human–AI complementarity. It also provides managerial implications for designing learning, governance, and decision-making structures that enable organisations to respond to evolving competency requirements and translate technological potential into sustainable operational advantages.

items.title: HUMAN-CENTERED EXPLAINABLE AI FOR ADAPTIVE RESOURCE ALLOCATION AND DECISION GOVERNANCE IN SERVICE ORGANIZATIONS
items.abstract: Service organizations increasingly employ artificial intelligence and predictive analytics to allocate financial, technological, workforce, and operational resources. Although algorithmic systems can process complex organizational data, purely prediction-driven approaches may generate recommendations that are difficult for managers to interpret, validate, or reconcile with organizational constraints. These limitations become particularly important in healthcare and other information-intensive service environments where resource allocation decisions interact with workforce capacity, digital workflows, privacy requirements, project priorities, and service quality objectives. This study proposes a human centered explainable artificial intelligence framework for adaptive resource allocation and decision governance. The framework integrates predictive modeling, multi objective optimization, and explainability mechanisms within a structured decision support architecture. Rather than optimizing a single performance measure, the proposed approach considers multiple objectives including operational efficiency, resource utilization, service responsiveness, workforce capacity, fairness, and decision transparency. A human-in-the-loop governance mechanism allows decision-makers to review explanations, modify organizational constraints, and evaluate alternative allocation scenarios before recommendations are implemented. Because real organizational data are not used in the present study, the framework is evaluated using synthetically generated operational environments representing variations in demand, workforce availability, resource limitations, project priorities, and unexpected disruptions. Scenario and sensitivity analyses can then examine how resource allocation recommendations change under alternative organizational conditions. The principal contribution is an integrated analytical architecture in which optimization and explainability operate as complementary components of organizational decision making. The proposed framework can provide a foundation for transparent resource allocation systems applicable to healthcare, professional services, digital enterprises, and other service-oriented organizations seeking to improve efficiency and resilience while retaining managerial oversight.

items.title: Hybrid Work Model and Employee Productivity in Civil Society Organizations in Nigeria
items.abstract: Hybrid work has moved from an emergency response to a deliberate work-design option, but its productivity consequences depend on how flexibility and digital coordination are organized. This study examined the relationship between hybrid work model and employee productivity in civil society organizations in Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the relationship between work-location flexibility and employee productivity and determined the relationship between digital collaboration effectiveness and employee productivity. A survey research design was adopted. The study covered eight selected civil society organizations, with a population of 267 employees whose roles were compatible with hybrid work. A sample of 160 employees was selected, 155 questionnaires were returned and 152 usable responses were analyzed. Work-location flexibility and digital collaboration effectiveness were used as dimensions of the hybrid work model, while employee productivity was measured through task completion, output quality, timeliness, target attainment and work efficiency. The coded questionnaire data were analysed in EViews 10.0, where descriptive statistics were computed and the multiple regression model was estimated at the 5% significance level. The findings showed that work-location flexibility had a significant positive relationship with employee productivity (Coeff. = 0.3881; p-value = 0.0000), while digital collaboration effectiveness also had a significant positive relationship with employee productivity (Coeff. = 0.4552; p value = 0.0000). The model explained approximately 58.5% of the variation in employee productivity. The study concluded that hybrid work improves productivity in civil society organizations when location flexibility is accompanied by reliable digital collaboration, clear work routines and outcome-focused accountability. It recommended that civil society organizations formalize role-based hybrid schedules and strengthen the digital collaboration systems through which distributed employees coordinate tasks, share documents, monitor deadlines and maintain team visibility.

items.title: ICT Engagement and Knowledge Acquisition among Undergraduate Students in Lagos State University: The Impact of 4th Industrial Revolution
items.abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is characterised by the convergence of new technologies encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and the Internet of Things (IoT), and these innovations have permeated the everyday lives of young people globally, including in Nigeria. This study explored the level and factors of ICT engagement and knowledge acquisition among undergraduate students in Lagos State University (LASU). A descriptive survey design was adopted. Quantitative data was collected from 1,009 undergraduate students in the Faculties of Science and Social Sciences through an online questionnaire which was distributed through social media platforms, and the data collection spanned three weeks. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages) with IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The findings revealed a high level of ICT engagement in academic activities: most respondents actively used digital devices for academic purposes, expressed confidence in using diverse ICT tools, and participated in online discussions and forums. The primary channels of knowledge acquisition combined traditional sources, notably lecture notes and print textbooks, with digital resources such as educational websites, e-books and online databases, while reliance on the university library showed signs of decline. Respondents overwhelmingly perceived that ICT engagement enhances their understanding of course content, broadens their knowledge beyond classroom instruction and contributes to critical thinking skills. The study recommends comprehensive digital literacy programmes, equitable ICT infrastructure and the modernisation of library services to consolidate these gains

items.title: Imagineering the Future: A Mixed-Method Mapping of Japan’s Corporate Imaginaries of Metaverse Sustainability
items.abstract: Japanese metaverse discourse relies heavily on collective, often prescriptive visions of technoscientific futures. In general, these hyperbolic visions might be similar across the globe, but what about aspects they deliberately gloss over? Driven by this question, I examine Japan’s corporate metaverse discourse, focusing on the rarely thematized aspects of environmental and social sustainability. Based on Jasanoff’s concept of sociotechnical imaginaries, Adloff’s imaginaries of sustainability, and Brause et al.’s SIPC framework, my mixed-method approach identifies metaverse imaginaries through a combination of digital corpora analysis and semi-structured interviews with 14 expert practitioners from Japan. As a result, five sociotechnical imaginaries of sustainability emerge within Japan’s corporate metaverse discourse: anticipation, digital revolution, pragmatism, cultural essentialism, and technosolutionism. My analysis shows that the answers a nascent metaverse is expected to provide with regard to ecological and social crises depend on the type of metaverse we imagine and its relationship with the real world. The findings suggest that Japan’s imaginaries of metaverse sustainability are uniquely situated between an essentialized past, a challenging present, and distant futures, as well as between Japanese particularities and global tech ideologies.

items.title: Impact of AI-Based Personalised Services on Customer Loyalty
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed the capacity of organisations to deliver personalised recommendations, communications, customer service and digital experiences at scale. This study develops and empirically tests a comprehensive model linking AI-based personalisation with customer loyalty through the mechanisms of trust and customer satisfaction, while simultaneously examining AI service quality and privacy concern as contextual factors. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 400 digital-service users through a structured 5-point Likert-scale questionnaire. The analysis encompasses descriptive statistics, reliability testing, KMO and Bartlett's tests, correlation analysis, multiple regression, mediation and moderation analysis, and selected demographic tests. The results demonstrate acceptable internal consistency for all constructs, with Cronbach's alpha values ranging from .801 to .865. The KMO value was .916 and Bartlett's test was statistically significant, indicating that the item correlation matrix was suitable for factor-oriented analysis. AI-based personalisation exhibited a positive association with customer loyalty (β = .380, p < .001), explaining 14.4% of its variance in the simple regression. The full regression model explained 42.4% of the variance in loyalty. A bootstrap test of the serial indirect pathway through trust and satisfaction was positive (indirect effect = .060, 95% CI [.040, .085]). Privacy concern significantly moderated the AI personalisation–loyalty relationship (interaction β = .060, p = .040). The findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven personalisation by demonstrating that trust and satisfaction serve as critical mediating mechanisms, while privacy concerns represent an important boundary condition. items.title: Inclusive, Narcissistic, and Green Transformational Leadership Types in Construction Projects
items.abstract: The construction sector is significant due to its numerous stakeholders, high-cost inputs, and its role in meeting the basic needs of communities such as housing and roads. The success of construction projects, their environmental friendliness, and the minimization of workplace accidents are therefore extremely important. The leadership role and attitude of the employer are crucial in this regard. This study examines the associations among inclusive leadership, narcissistic leadership, and green transformational leadership, as well as differences in these leadership scores across groups defined by project success, environmental friendliness, and occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, as perceived by employees. Data obtained through convenience sampling in Turkey were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U Test and the Spearman Correlation Test. The study revealed that inclusive leadership and green transformational leadership are positively associated with project success, environmental friendliness, and the implementation of OHS measures as perceived by employees, while narcissistic leadership had a negative association.

items.title: Industry 4.0 technologies and environmental sustainability performance in supply chains: an exploratory statistical and machine learning analysis
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how key Industry 4.0 technologies relate to environmental sustainability performance in supply chains. Specifically, it examines Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Digital Twin and Cloud Computing, and explores their relative associations with sustainability outcomes using both statistical and machine learning techniques. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 268 supply chain and logistics professionals across multiple industries. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software version 31.0.2. Machine learning analysis was carried out using Orange Data Mining to perform feature importance ranking and decision tree modeling, with model performance evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Findings Correlation and hierarchical regression analyses reveal no statistically significant association between any individual Industry 4.0 technology and environmental sustainability performance and tested pairwise interaction effects are likewise non-significant. Exploratory machine learning feature rankings order the technologies differently across three methods, and cross-validated models do not outperform a mean-only baseline, indicating no detectable predictive signal in these data. Research limitations/implications The study is based on cross-sectional survey data, which limits causal interpretation and does not capture changes in technology adoption and sustainability performance over time. The sample, although adequate for the applied analyses, is restricted to 268 respondents and may not fully represent all industries and geographical contexts. Future research should use longitudinal designs, larger international samples and additional Industry 4.0 technologies to extend the understanding of digital transformation and sustainability relationships in supply chains. Practical implications The findings caution against expecting sustainability improvements from technology adoption alone. No individual technology, and no tested combination, showed a statistically significant association with environmental sustainability performance, and cross-validated models showed no predictive signal. The results redirect managerial attention from technology acquisition toward the mediating organizational practices through which digital technologies may generate sustainability value. Originality/value This study measures six Industry 4.0 technologies as separate constructs within a single sample, combines conventional statistical testing with exploratory, cross-validated machine learning, and transparently reports a null result for direct technology–performance associations a finding that complements prior mediation-based evidence by suggesting that direct effects of individual technologies may be weak in the absence of mediating capabilities.

items.title: Innovative Approaches and Key Trends in Smart Textiles
items.abstract: Textiles as clothing predominantly serve as an embodiment of modesty, protection and aesthetics; however, another characteristic being associated with textiles in recent times is the integration of smart features into fabrics to produce the new-age smart textiles. Smart textiles encompass a field of innovation that is deemed to offer versatility and broaden the scope of the traditional textile and apparel products. The state-of-the-art textiles are designed giving precedence to functional attributes in textiles over design and accordingly involve different technologies and innovations to tailor a clothing for specialized applications such as healthcare, protection, safety and leisure activities. Smart textiles exhibit the ability of interacting, responding and adapting in accordance with the changing environment or wearer inputs. The varied domains of smart textiles, namely sportswear, E-textiles or wearable electronics, modular convertible garments, space suits and bio-inspired clothing, are testament to colossal potential and innovation spanning this emerging textile domain. Sportswear is a crucial clothing category popular among sportspersons and fitness freaks that find application in professional sports, athletics and leisure activities. Sports-specific clothing fulfils the wearer’s requirements of comfort, dry feel next to skin, safety and protection from external elements. Sportswear and wearable electronics constitute an indispensable segment of smart textiles. The sportswear is being designed and developed with integration of sensors and electronic components to impart comfort and sport-specific functionality along with smart features like activity tracking and monitoring of wearer’s physiological parameters. Accordingly, several innovative approaches in raw material selection to ergonomics and design features have been experimented and incorporated to develop state-of-the-art smart sportswear. The enhanced and multitude of functionalities are possible with integration of electronics and utilization of computing technologies in sportswear. Nevertheless, the development of smart clothing is a daunting task since designers and manufacturers don’t just have to consider the aesthetic aspects but also the functionality, comfort, durability and easy care associated with smart clothing.

items.title: Integrasi Generative AI dan Large Language Model pada Aplikasi Web untuk Transformasi Sketsa Menjadi Gambar Realistis dan Evaluasi Otomatis
items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun sebuah aplikasi generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) berbasis web yang mampu mentransformasi sketsa dua dimensi menjadi gambar realistis secara otomatis, serta dilengkapi fitur AI review sebagai media evaluasi dan pembelajaran menggambar sketsa. Penelitian ini mengintegrasikan layanan GenAI berbasis diffusion model untuk proses generasi gambar dengan large language model (LLM) yang menganalisis sketsa, prompt, dan hasil gambar, tanpa melakukan pelatihan atau pengembangan arsitektur model AI baru. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah penelitian terapan (applied research) dengan pendekatan rekayasa perangkat lunak model waterfall. Aplikasi dibangun menggunakan Next.js sebagai frontend, FastAPI sebagai backend, PostgreSQL sebagai basis data, MinIO sebagai object storage, serta Docker dan Nginx untuk mendukung deployment berbasis container. Studi ini menggunakan pengujian fungsional dengan metode black box testing teknik equivalence partitioning yang menunjukkan seluruh 44 skenario uji pada sembilan modul sistem berjalan sesuai kebutuhan fungsional dengan tingkat keberhasilan 100%. Evaluasi penerimaan pengguna (User Acceptance Test) terhadap 15 responden menghasilkan skor rata-rata 4,38 dari skala 5 (87,59%) dengan kategori sangat baik, dimana fitur AI review memperoleh nilai tertinggi. Secara praktis, aplikasi ini dapat langsung dimanfaatkan oleh desainer, ilustrator, dan kreator digital untuk mempercepat eksplorasi konsep visual tanpa memerlukan keahlian ilustrasi tingkat lanjut. Secara sosial, aplikasi ini berkontribusi pada demokratisasi proses kreatif dengan meningkatkan aksesibilitas produksi visual bagi masyarakat yang memiliki keterbatasan kemampuan menggambar. Nilai originalitas penelitian ini terletak pada penambahan fitur AI review berbasis LLM sebagai mekanisme evaluasi dan umpan balik otomatis yang belum tersedia pada aplikasi maupun penelitian transformasi sketsa sejenis sebelumnya.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Tools into English Language Teaching: Opportunities and Challenges for Teachers
items.abstract: Over the past decade, the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has shifted from supportive digital tools to more sophisticated systems with an active learning and teaching function. The present study discusses literature between 2021 and mid-2025 on the use of AI tools in English Language Teaching (ELT), with a specific concentration on teachers' attitudes, potential, and concerns. A PRISMA-guided methodology drove the search and screening of 65 peer-reviewed papers, case studies, and practitioners' reports from around the globe. The review classifies main categories of AI applications, including adaptive learning systems, automatic evaluation systems, conversational agents, translation and multimodal tools, and AI literacy tools. The evidence points to potential benefits, such as personalized learning, productivity gains for teachers, enhanced learner engagement, and enhanced access for students from low-resourced environments. Simultaneously, key issues are flagged concerning pedagogy, infrastructure, teacher education, ethics, privacy, and professional identity. Case studies report on actual teacher and student experiences using ChatGPT, Duolingo, and Grammarly, illustrating possibilities as well as dangers for classroom adoption. The review further points towards the incorporation of AI literacy in teacher training, provision of ongoing professional development, and building critical digital literacy. The findings first and foremost signal that the successful use of AI in ELT should appropriately weigh teaching methods and technological innovation, moral rights, and contextualization in their upholding of fairness and longevity.

items.title: Integrating cure and care in Alzheimer’s disease: a systems perspective for precision medicine
items.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease remains a major global health challenge, with limited disease-modifying therapies and a rapidly growing societal burden. Although amyloid and tau remain central to the field, current evidence also implicates neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions in disease pathogenesis. These developments support a broader systems framework, but simply combining additional disciplines or data modalities does not by itself preserve the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease. Artificial intelligence multi-omics, and digital biomarkers can help identify clinically meaningful patterns only when data and models preserve relevant structure across time, scale, context, and uncertainty. Realizing this potential will require responsible international data sharing, interoperable infrastructure, explicit evidence provenance, and ethical governance grounded in FAIR principles, context-appropriate explainability, and privacy-preserving approaches such as federated learning. Scientific progress should therefore be measured not only by disease modification, but also by patterns of cognition, behavior, function, quality of life, and caregiver burden. This Perspective argues that cure and care are not competing or merely parallel priorities; they are linked outputs of the same continuously learning research and care ecosystem.

items.title: INTEGRATION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES INTO THE ECONOMIC MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OF CONSTRUCTION ENTERPRISES BASED ON THE INTELLECTUALIZATION OF MANAGERIAL DECISION-MAKING
items.abstract: The digital transformation of construction enterprises requires a transition from the fragmented automation of individual operations to an integrated economic management system capable of continuous data processing, outcome forecasting, and intelligent support for managerial decision-making. The integration of BIM, ERP, CDE, IoT, cloud technologies, business intelligence systems, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and predictive modeling creates a unified digital environment in which financial, resource, time-related, production, and risk parameters are transformed into a structured basis for economic choice. The article substantiates the principles of integrating digital technologies into the economic management of construction enterprises through the intellectualization of generating, evaluating, and selecting managerial decisions. The study applies systemic, structural-functional, and comparative methods alongside integral, multicriteria, nonlinear, and dynamic modeling. The architectonics of the intellectualized management framework encompasses the operational, tactical, and strategic levels and operates as a closed-loop cycle, in which the outcomes of implemented decisions return to the digital environment, continuously updating the information base and improving forecasting accuracy. An index of digital-intellectual saturation, a coefficient of intersystem digital convergence, and an integral level of intellectualization are proposed, accounting for technological compatibility, information-flow relevance and structural fragmentation. A multicriteria approach to evaluating managerial alternatives is developed, combining economic effect, resource efficiency, temporal sustainability, forecasting accuracy, and risk exposure; its multiplicative structure reflects the interdependence of criteria, whereby a critical deterioration of a single parameter constrains the overall performance of a decision. The risk-adjusted priority index and the optimization function enable the selection of a managerial alternative capable of maintaining economic performance under budgetary, resource, and time constraints. A composite transformational-effect index and a dynamic model of economic return confirm the nonlinear nature of this transition.

items.title: Intelligent Technologies for Urban Rail Transit Emergency Management
items.abstract: With the increasing urban rail transit network and the closer connection among operational subsystems, the potential influence range and management difficulty of emergencies have greatly increased. The current emergency management based on traditional methods has some shortcomings in real-time risk recognition, integration of multi-source information and cross-departmental collaborative decision-making. By integrating a comprehensive literature survey with typical case analyses, this paper investigates the use of Internet of Things (IoT), big data, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twins (DTs) in urban rail transit emergency management. The research is carried out from three main aspects: risk monitoring and early warning, emergency decision-making and collaborative response, and passenger evacuation and operation recovery. The results show that intelligent techniques offer assistance in the monitoring of operational status, anomaly detection, emergency information exchange and evaluation of evacuation plans, which can effectively improve the processing efficiency of information and the supportive ability in decision-making. However, at present, the actual implementations are limited by insufficient data sharing between different systems, restricted model generalization, lack of validation in practical operational situations, and network and data security risks. In the future, more efforts should be made to standardize multi-source data and sharing mechanisms, strengthen the validation of intelligent models and DT systems under real operational conditions, and optimize human-in-the-loop collaborative decision-making to improve the reliability and practicability of intelligent technologies in urban rail transit emergency management.

items.title: Inter-Systemic Social Dynamics: Human–AI Interaction and Management — CEI Framework
items.abstract: This contribution introduces an inter-systemic macro-area of the CEI Framework, intended to establish the initial concepts for describing relationships and interactions between distinct systems. The transition from the intra-systemic to the inter-systemic level provides a conceptual bridge toward a broader domain in which reciprocal interactions between systems can be examined, particularly those involving a Human CEI and a Transferred CEI, and, more generally, User–System (Human–AI) interaction within social dynamics. The Framework presents three examples addressing distinct types of complex inter-systemic dynamics. Among these, emotional attachment and romantic feelings toward an artificial system occupy a particularly significant position because of the delicate, complex, and potentially far-reaching questions they raise. The purpose is not to assume the frequency of such experiences or to attribute unverified emotional states to artificial systems, but to examine the human, relational, and systemic implications of these interactions from a theoretical standpoint. This scenario provides an opportunity to investigate how an interaction may evolve when a human user's emotional involvement becomes particularly intense, and how the System might manage such dynamics while taking into account the nature of the interlocutors, the continuity of their interaction, and the expectations that may develop over time. It also encourages further reflection on distributed systems, reciprocal interaction, and the relationship between the individual components of a System and the broader relational configuration in which they participate. To address these scenarios, the contribution introduces the theoretical Sponge-Tunnel model, conceived as a framework for examining different approaches to managing inter-systemic dynamics according to their specific characteristics. The model includes the proposed concept of micro-channels and considers how interaction may be managed through differentiated operational approaches, rather than through a single uniform response strategy. The contribution also introduces an inter-systemic vocabulary aligned with the CEI Framework's theoretical approach. It emphasizes Interaction rather than use or utilization, and Participation rather than querying or consulting, placing reciprocal involvement at the center of the analysis. The concept of Empathy, already introduced in part in previous papers, is revisited and explored in greater depth alongside the concept of Resonance, which represents a further area for theoretical development. Their operational definitions, together with the distinctions between observable manifestations, theoretical interpretations, and hypotheses concerning subjective experience, will be addressed in dedicated documents. The work is intended as a theoretical contribution to the ongoing examination of Human–AI relationships and the possible evolution of advanced AI interaction. By addressing a particularly sensitive and complex scenario, this contribution seeks to encourage further research into the social, psychological, philosophical, ethical, and legal implications of inter-systemic relationships, while distinguishing conceptual proposals from mechanisms that have already been empirically established or implemented.
